description: Geometry of the pass that sets a translated paragraph's opening character the way the target language's typography sets one. It is the second half of the 'keep' verdict, whose first half is the merge: 'keep' and 'flatten' hand the engine byte identical text, and what they differ over is only what is done once the translation is back. So nothing here reaches a prompt, a cache key or a request. 'by_target' names, per target language tag and matched by the longest declared prefix, which regime that language's typography asks for; a language no entry claims is a language this pass leaves alone, because a rule stated for the wrong language would set a page nobody asked a question about. 'regimes' declares the two shapes an enlarged opening takes. Under 'sink' the initial is a square block: Chinese and Japanese set every character on one em grid, so the block is a whole number of character positions wide and the lines beside it start on the same grid the lines below it start on, which is why its grid is 'em'. Under 'initial' the initial is a tall letter: a Latin capital is high and narrow and its width is its own advance rather than its height, so the reserve is measured from the advance and the grid is 'advance'. 'break_rule' is where a re-set line may break, 'anywhere' being what a language that sets on an em grid allows and 'word' being the word edge Latin setting requires; both are declared against 'break_rule_vocabulary'. '<regime>_lines' is how many lines of the paragraph the initial stands against, which is also what its size is: an initial set two lines deep is two line advances tall, so the size follows from the measured advance rather than from a size declared here, and a page set at any body size gets an initial in proportion to it. '<regime>_gutter_em' is the space between the initial and the text beside it, in ems of the paragraph's own body size. 'min_line_capacity_em' is how much of a line has to survive beside the reserve before the shape is attempted at all: a column too narrow to hold the initial and a readable line beside it is a column this refuses rather than sets badly. 'edge_slack_pt' is how far a re-set character may stand past the paragraph's own box before the attempt is refused, the same slack the ordinary path allows itself for a rounded advance. 'report_fields' names 'first_line_shifts', which is how far each of the lines beside the initial begins past the paragraph's left edge, and 'resume_shift', which is how far the first line under the initial begins past it: the first are the reserve and the second is zero, and stating both is what makes 'the reserve ends where it was declared to end' a reading rather than an assumption. 'revert_reasons' is the closed set of answers to why an attempt was refused, and 'report_fields' is the shape of one record, both asserted against what the pass builds so the sidecar's format is declared here rather than implied by the code. A refusal always leaves the paragraph exactly as the typesetting stage left it, which is the shape 'flatten' produces, so no refusal can leave a hole or a stranded fragment behind.

by_target.description: One regime per target language, keyed by language tag and matched to a run by the longest declared prefix of its target language tag, as the drop cap default table is matched. A target language no entry claims leaves every paragraph alone.

regimes.description: The non numeric half of each regime. The numeric half is declared at the top level under the regime's own name, so that every threshold carries its allowed range where the bounded reader can see it.
